meta.title: Boxuan Shi
meta.description: Data scientist. Carnegie Mellon, Dec 2026. Forecasting, causal inference, and applied ML.

profile.name: Boxuan Shi
bio: I build models meant to survive contact with production — budget forecasting across three thousand cost centers, revenue diagnostics on auction data, credit scoring that a regulator could read.
Lately I have been building FIND, an internship matching platform, mostly to find out what breaks when you run the whole stack yourself.

education.degree: Master of Information Systems Management — Business Intelligence and Data Analytics
Bachelor of Mgmt. in Digital Accounting

experience.role: Data Scientist Intern, Applied AI Team
highlights: Built a production-bound Travel & Entertainment budget forecasting model for the Finance organization across ~3,000 cost centers with 40 months of history; reduced forecast error ~8% on RMSE and ~17% on WAPE vs. baseline, and ~33% vs. human planners on both metrics.

Engineered a threshold-based hybrid of two XGBoost models — standard L2 for high-spend transactions, and a log-L2 objective with sign classifier for the small, intermittent ones — to hold accuracy across a wide spend range; applied Tree SHAP to make each forecast explainable to Finance stakeholders.

experience.role: Data Scientist Intern, Greater China Region Data Insight Team
highlights: Diagnosed revenue leakage in an APAC Ads storefront by analyzing the revenue funnel and auction-level bid data with SQL (Athena, Snowflake) and PySpark; identified ~6% unfilled searches and surfaced high-potential keywords by scoring demand signals. Contributed to keyword coverage and brand protection strategies projected to drive ~15% uplift in annual revenue; reported to management across two milestones.

Built a client-value model using linear regression with Scikit-learn on ~25 demographic and funnel features to estimate revenue headroom; visualized key insights with Matplotlib and Seaborn and delivered ranked client lists to Sales, improving pitch success rate by ~10%.

experience.role: Fintech Data Scientist Intern, Intelligent Stock Team
highlights: Designed a Python/SQL ELTL pipeline processing 4,000+ stocks across 150 metrics daily for a market-monitor product; built a reusable multithreading decorator for concurrent query execution (5x speedup).

Built credit scoring models in Python (NumPy, Pandas) for 18 industries using Genetic Algorithm optimization with custom constraints — category-level feature cardinality, weight caps, and a penalty for sign violations — to ensure interpretability; used Somers' D as the objective function, saving 10 person-days in project delivery.

projects.name: FIND
projects.subtitle: Internship Matching Platform
highlights: Developed an ML/AI-driven internship matching platform; gained 57 users within two weeks of beta. Built 66 crawlers monitoring ~19,000 active internship opportunities, with Prometheus and Grafana dashboards tracking system health, key metrics, and data drift.

Integrated the DeepSeek LLM for resume parsing, job match reasoning, and cover letter generation — with prompt-injection protection and PII masking. Designed a bilingual semantic matching algorithm using a BGE-M3 encoder and pgvector, with a sigmoid to curve the matching score.

Designed and ran a randomized landing-page experiment (50/50 block randomization, pre-specified ATE and HTE, covariate balance checks, power analysis) testing whether previewing sample output raises resume-upload intent; the effect was directionally positive with no moderation by privacy concern, and the sample-first onboarding flow shipped.

research.title: Impact of Image in ESG Reports on ESG Performance
research.advisor: Supervised by Zhang, Qi at Harbin Institute of Technology, Weihai
highlights: Built a multimodal analysis pipeline processing 11,000+ corporate ESG reports: automated PDF parsing for text and image extraction, and image-text semantic similarity computed with OpenAI CLIP.
Discovered a U-shaped relationship between image density and ESG performance (inflection ~2.3 images/page), amplified by image-text alignment, using GLS regression with random effects in Stata.
